Prevention: Plant clean seedlings free from infestation.
Use a shade net (size 400 µm) or tunnel for 3-5 weeks while in the nursery to prevent attack by whiteflies.
Conserve natural enemies (wasps and ladybirds) by leaving a natural hedge of flowering plants along the edges to offer them refuge.
Transplant shortly after or during the rainy season.
Plant repellent crops such as coriander or
Mexican marigold every 3-4 rows of tomato to repel the whiteflies.
Plant trap crops, such as beans and maize, around the field.
Keep the field weed-free throughout the cropping season since weeds act as alternate hosts.
Monitoring: Whitish-brown eggs laid in a spiral pattern and/or whitish adults on the underside of young leaves. 3-5 white insects that resettle soon after the plant is shaken.
Yellowing on the upper leaf surface.
Start direct control if 3 adult whiteflies are present when the plant is shaken during the early stages of the crop.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Use yellow sticky traps to bait adults (16 traps per quarter acre).
Use liquid soap spray at a rate of 3 tablespoons per litre of water.
Use hot pepper spray: add 30 chopped peppers to warm water.
Soak for 1 day, dilute in 10L water, and add 20 drops of liquid soap before spraying.

Direct Control (Chemical): When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing.
Always consult a recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, and restricted re-entry intervals.
